Notice the shape it looks like a bowl . A function is convex if it curves upward everywhere. Visually: draw a straight line between any two points on the curve the curve always stays below that line.

A convex function has exactly one minimum no bumps, no extra dips. That s what makes it possible to find the bottom reliably.

fragments.text: You probably compared each prediction to the real value and picked the line with the smallest errors . Line A has zero error everywhere it s a perfect fit. You just invented a loss function : a single number that measures how bad a line is. Now how exactly should we compute that number?

slide_text: For each point, the error is: prediction [math] actual [math]. But some errors are positive and some negative they cancel if you just add them. How would you fix the cancellation problem? Think of at least one way to make all errors positive before adding them.

fragments.text: Two common ideas: take the absolute value of each error, or square each error. Both work! Squaring is more common it penalizes large errors more heavily and is smoother (easier for gradient descent).

slide_text: Your turn: Write a formula that squares each error and takes the mean.

fragments.text: [math] This is called Mean Squared Error (MSE) . A smaller MSE means a better fit. MSE = 0 means the line passes through every point.
